title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description: You get the heads of two linked lists, each sorted in non-decreasing order. Splice their nodes together into a single sorted list and return its head.
hints: Think of the classic merge step from merge sort: compare the two front elements and take the smaller.
Edge handling (empty lists, which node becomes the head) gets messy. A placeholder node at the start removes those special cases.
Use a dummy node and a tail pointer. While both lists have nodes, attach the smaller one and advance it. Afterwards attach whichever list still has nodes. Return dummy.next.
starterCode:
class Solution:
    def mergeTwoLists(self, list1: Optional[ListNode], list2: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:

solution.explanation: Create a dummy head and a tail pointer. While both lists are non-empty, link the node with the smaller value to the tail, advance that list and the tail. When one list is exhausted, link the remainder of the other, since it is already sorted. Return dummy.next. Each node is visited once: O(n + m) time, O(1) extra space because nodes are reused.
